translations.Repository Treemap Tooltip Body: The repository treemap shows each file and folder as a rectangle whose area is proportional to its relative size in the repository (typically by lines of code or file size). Larger areas indicate files or folders that take up more of the repository. Double-click a folder to drill down into its internal structure; single-click to select it and view the commit and author statistics on the right. Colors distinguish folders, and a darker border marks the currently selected item.

translations.A quick tour of the essentials — the too: A quick tour of the essentials — the toolbar, sidebar, history and commit area — plus power features like git mm, the repository treemap, the reflog timeline and AI conflict resolution. Takes just a couple of minutes.
translations.Pull fetches and integrates remote chang: Pull fetches and integrates remote changes, Push publishes your local commits, and Branch creates or switches branches. The badges on the buttons show how many commits you are ahead or behind.
translations.The sidebar on the left lists your local: The sidebar on the left lists your local branches, tags and remotes. Click a branch to switch to it, and use the right-click menu to track, merge, rebase or delete branches.
translations.The revision graph shows the full histor: The revision graph shows the full history of the active branch. Click a commit to inspect it: the details pane below shows exactly what changed, file by file, with syntax-colored diffs.
Your changes appear in the changes list. Stage the files you want, write a subject and a description, then hit Commit. AI can draft the commit message for you from the staged changes.
translations.That's the basics. You can revisit this: That's the basics. You can revisit this tour anytime via Help > Getting Started, and customize themes, languages and everything else in Preferences. Happy committing!
translations.ForkPlus ships with git mm built in: a l: ForkPlus ships with git mm built in: a lean workflow that keeps a main repository and its sub repositories in sync. Switch to the git mm workspace, then use Sync git mm to pull all sub repos consistently or Upload git mm to push their changes together (requires git-mm 3.x).
translations.Open Repository Treemap... for a size ma: Open Repository Treemap... for a size map of your repository: every rectangle is a file or folder, sized by its footprint on disk. Click a rectangle to drill down into a folder and discover what really eats your space.
translations.Repository Statistics... counts code, co: Repository Statistics... counts code, comments and blank lines per language — powered by tokei with support for 200+ languages — and visualizes the mix as a pie chart. Switch the ref between workspace, branch or tag to compare.
translations.The Reflog keeps a timeline rail of ever: The Reflog keeps a timeline rail of every operation performed in ForkPlus: commits, checkouts, resets and more. Open it from the toolbar, then double-click an entry to jump back to that earlier state — safely, with undo.
translations.When a merge or rebase hits conflicts, t: When a merge or rebase hits conflicts, the affected files appear in the commit view. Resolve them line by line in the side-by-side merger, pick a version from the context menu, or let AI resolve all conflicts in one click.
translations.Make ForkPlus yours: 12 built-in themes: Make ForkPlus yours: 12 built-in themes — from Light and Dark to Dracula, Monokai and Solarized — plus custom colors, 8 interface languages, and a tab bar you can place at the top or on the left. Everything lives in Preferences and switches instantly.
